mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the discount rate applied to equity valuations and encourage risk-taking.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return in the lowest FEDFUNDS quartile is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL value above 245.0 signals persistent inflation, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day S&P 500 return is positive when CPIAUCSL > 245.0 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) and strong GDP growth (GDPC1 > 16800.0) signals an overheating economy, prompting aggressive monetary tightening by the Fed and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day S&P 500 return is positive when UNRATE < 4.0% and GDPC1 > 16800.0 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising at least 0.5% in the past 3 months), the S&P 500 tends to have negative forward returns over the next 20 days due to increased discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: The average 20-day S&P 500 return is positive during periods when FEDFUNDS rises >= 0.5% in 3 months over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 indicates a weakening economy, prompting monetary easing and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as the market prices in recession risks.
failure_condition: The average 5-day S&P 500 return is positive when INDPRO < 100.0 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.0%) indicates economic distress, prompting aggressive monetary easing and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day S&P 500 return is negative when UNRATE > 5.0% over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) and high industrial production (INDPRO > 105.0) signals an overheating economy, prompting aggressive monetary tightening and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day S&P 500 return is positive when UNRATE < 4.0% and INDPRO > 105.0 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary easing cycle (FEDFUNDS falling at least 0.5% in the past 3 months), the S&P 500 tends to have positive forward returns over the next 60 days as lower rates boost equity valuations and economic activity.
failure_condition: The average 60-day S&P 500 return is negative during periods when FEDFUNDS falls <= -0.5% in 3 months over the last 5 years.
